device.description: 12-bit single-channel ultralow-glitch voltage-output DAC with 50 MHz SPI interface, IOVDD level shifters, daisy-chain SDO and asynchronous clear
device.note: dac7551.pdf (SLAS441E) p.4 power requirements (VDD 2.7-5.5 V, IOVDD 1.8 V-VDD), p.5 pin configuration and pin descriptions, p.6 serial write operation (Figure 1) and timing characteristics (t9 SDO valid 10 ns), p.12 asynchronous clear, IOVDD, power-on reset (zero), p.13 serial interface (16-bit word latched at SYNC rising: last 16 bits), daisy-chain SDO, Table 1

registers.name: DAC
registers.note: DAC register: power-on reset clears it (zero scale), p.12

registers.name: CTRL
registers.note: internal: PD1/PD0 (DB13/DB12) of the last word, Table 1 (00 normal mode)

registers.name: SR
registers.note: internal: the 16-bit input shift register as latched (its contents are shifted out on SDO at the next SYNC low)

commands.name: WRITE
commands.note: Table 1: DB15-DB14 don't care, DB13-DB12 PD1/PD0, DB11-DB0 data; the last 16 bits before SYNC rises are latched and the DAC updates at SYNC rising (p.13)

pages: p.4 (power requirements), p.5 (pins), p.6 (timing, Figure 1), p.12 (clear, IOVDD, power-on reset), p.13 (serial interface, daisy chain, Table 1)
notModeled: analog output, unbuffered VREFH/VREFL reference, VFB sense input (never driven)
power-down output loads (1 kOhm / 100 kOhm / Hi-Z): PD1/PD0 stored in CTRL.PD only; Table 1 marks the data bits don't care in power-down, the model still writes them
SDO repeats SDIN with a 16-clock delay while SYNC is low: modeled as the previously latched 16-bit word (SR) followed by Hi-Z; words longer than 32 bits in one SYNC frame are not repeated
CLR resets all registers and the DAC updates at the first SYNC rising edge after CLR returns high (p.12): modeled as an immediate clear to code 0
SCLK limits (50 MHz, 10 MHz with SDO) and setup/hold times
variants: single-channel member of the DAC7551/DAC7552/DAC7558 family (daisy-chainable together, dac7558.pdf p.21); the pin drawing on p.5 is captioned DAC7751 (typo).
